Michael surveys $50$ randomly chosen adults that visited a park. He asked about their favorite activity between reading and walking. His findings are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Prefers Reading | Prefers Walking | Totals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Female | $12$ | $8$ | $20$ |
| Male | $12$ | $18$ | $30$ |
| Totals | $24$ | $26$ | $50$ |

Let $M$ be the event that a randomly selected person visiting the park is a **"Male"**, and $R$ be the event that a randomly selected person visiting the park **"Prefers Reading"**. Estimate $P(M∩R)$.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

A survey asks the $8$th and $9$th graders in a school about whether they use social media. The findings are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Uses Social Media | Doesn't Use Social Media | Totals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8th grade | $60$ | $20$ | $80$ |
| 9th grade | $100$ | $20$ | $120$ |
| Totals | $160$ | $40$ | $200$ |

Let $A$ be the event that a randomly selected student is in **"$8$th grade"**, and $B$ be the event that a randomly selected student **"Uses Social Media"**. Estimate $P(A∩B)$.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

Some drinks of different sizes and flavors were sold during a school party. The two-way frequency table below summarizes the sold drinks.

|  | Soda | Water | Coca-Cola | Fanta | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Small | $6$ | $7$ | $9$ | $8$ | $30$ |
| Large | $5$ | $1$ | $7$ | $7$ | $20$ |
| Totals | $11$ | $8$ | $16$ | $15$ | $50$ |

Estimate the probability that a randomly selected sold drink is a small Fanta.

Rose surveyed $168$ children in Arizona High School. She asked them about their favorite topics in math, between geometry and algebra. Her findings are summarized in the two-way frequency table below. 

|  | Geometry | Algebra | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Girls | $28$ | $63$ | $91$ |
| Boys | $56$ | $21$ | $77$ |
| Totals | $84$ | $84$ | $168$ |

Let $B$ be the event that a randomly selected child is a **"Boy"** and $G$ the event that a randomly selected child likes **"Geometry"**. Estimate $P(B\cap G).$
